Pa- tients with restricted disease have a generally benign course, and single lesions often regress spontaneously. However, if a bone lesion does not resolve, or risks causing fracture or deformity before it resolves, or is causing disa- bling symptoms, it may be treated with curettage, intrale- sional corticosteroids, or radiotherapy.3-5,7 Systemic chem- otherapy may be suitable in some patients with multifocal bone disease; vinblastine with prednisone or prednisolone is a suggested regimen.4 Similarly, single skin lesions may be allowed to resolve without treatment or treated with surgery, topical corticosteroids, methoxsalen plus UV light (PUVA), or topical chlormethine.4,5 In more extensive disease the prognosis is not as good, mainly due to organ dysfunction.3,6,7 Systemic chemother- apy has been widely used, because the disease tends to be progressive in these patients, but its degree of benefit is uncertain.2,3,6,7 Corticosteroids and vinblastine for about 6 to 12 months are the most commonly used drugs; 6-mer- captopurine and methotrexate have also been used with re- ports of efficacy.4 A comparative study in children with multisystem disease found treatment with vinblastine or etoposide for 6 months to be equally effective.8 The over- all response rate was 62%, but about half of the patients had switched to the alternate arm or other therapy during the drug treatment period. Half of those patients who be- came disease-free did have a reactivation, but these were generally milder than the original disease. Patients who failed to respond within the first 6 weeks of therapy were at increased risk for treatment failure. Subsequent study showed that vinblastine with etoposide was not superior to vinblastine alone (when combined with corticosteroids and 6-mercaptopurine).4 Systemic corticosteroids have also been used for recalcitrant skin disease or multisystem disease in children9 and for pulmonary Langerhans-cell histiocytosis in adults.10 In patients who have not respond- ed to combination chemotherapy, a number of treatments may be considered including ciclosporin,4,7 the nucleoside analogues cladribine or pentostatin,11 thalidomide,9 and bone marrow transplantation.4,6,7 Anti-CD1 monoclonal antibodies5 may offer improved therapeutic or diagnostic options in the future. 1.
